title: Due Arduino Core
subtitle: autonomylogic:sam Arduino platform for the Arduino Due (C++14)
advisorySource: OSV via osv-scanner (lockfiles and requirements files only; this repository has none today)
_note_ids: Every triage entry lists the advisory ids it accounts for. build-report.mjs cross-checks the live post-suppression scan against these: an advisory no entry claims is reported in section 4a as untriaged instead of being silently omitted while the narrative implies full coverage.
_note_counts: advisories/counts describe the last FULL assessment (assessedAt) and are only rendered when the report is built without a live scan. With --osv-raw/--osv-delta the numbers come from that run.
headline: osv-scanner found no package manifest or lockfile to scan in this repository, so it reports no advisories. That is a statement about coverage, not a clean bill of health: the shipped platform is the upstream Arduino SAM core 1.6.12 plus Arduino's arm-none-eabi-gcc 7-2017q4 and bossac 1.6.1-arduino, none of which OSV indexes. They are listed in the SBOM and need a manual advisory review (see the scope note).
scope: This repository builds the autonomylogic:sam Arduino platform: tools/ci/build-release.py downloads Arduino's SAM core 1.6.12 at a pinned SHA-256, patches platform.txt and publishes the archive and the board manager index. The toolchain (arm-none-eabi-gcc 7-2017q4, with newlib linked into every sketch) and bossac are installed by the board manager from Arduino's own index.
scopeNote: The vulnerability scan covers package manifests and lockfiles only. The C/C++ code of the SAM core (Arduino API, USB stack, libsam, CMSIS), newlib and the toolchain binaries are inventoried in the SBOM from security/components.json but are not matched against any advisory database by this pipeline; OSV has no ecosystem for them. See security/README.md.
methodologyNote: Advisory data is obtained from OSV with osv-scanner, honouring the VEX baseline in osv-scanner.toml. The upstream core and the toolchain are pinned by version and SHA-256 in tools/ci/upstream.json and in Arduino's index, so the inventory is exact, but advisories for them (NVD CVEs for GCC, binutils, newlib) must be reviewed by hand.
licenseNote: The build scripts are GPL-3.0-only. The platform archive redistributes the upstream core under its per-file licences: LGPL-2.1-or-later (Arduino API, Wire), ISC (USB stack, HID), GPL-2.0-only OR LGPL-2.1-only (SPI), the Atmel SAM Software Package licence (libsam, CMSIS device files), the ARM CMSIS EULA and the LUFA 2010 licence. The toolchain is GPL-3.0-or-later WITH GCC-exception-3.1, so linking libgcc and libstdc++ into a sketch imposes no copyleft on it; newlib is under permissive per-file licences.
criticalNote: No critical advisory was reported by the scan, which covers package manifests only.
remediation: Manual review: check NVD for advisories against GCC 7.2.1, binutils 2.29, newlib 2.5.0 and bossac 1.6.1 when the toolchain pin changes.

practices.practice: Upstream core pinned by version and SHA-256 (tools/ci/upstream.json)
Platform archive installed and compiled before every release is published
Published index assets verified weekly (size and SHA-256)
SBOM generated per release in CycloneDX and SPDX
CI security gate on every pull request (new critical advisories)
That gate configured as a required status check, so it blocks the merge
Advisory matching for the C/C++ core and the toolchain
